speaker: Doctor
text: Dr. Agent: I need to understand the timeline of your symptoms; did the double vision appear before or after the weakness in your upper limbs? Also, does climbing stairs feel significantly harder than walking on a flat surface?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of symptoms worsening with activity and improving with rest is very telling. Do you experience any difficulty swallowing or speaking, and have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids? REQUEST TEST: CBC, Electrolytes, Creatine_Kinase. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the normal labs and MRI; since your symptoms fluctuate with activity and improve with rest, do you experience worsening weakness after prolonged use of your arms, and do you have a history of similar episodic episodes? REQUEST TEST: Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation, Single_Fiber_Electromyography, Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation: Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation; Single_Fiber_Electromyography: Not performed; Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated).

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of fluctuating weakness, ptosis, diplopia, and positive AChR antibodies confirms this diagnosis.
